prioritized_defects.description: The join/leave multicast notification branch is modeled as join/leave actions first and notification afterward, but the requirements specify that an agent sends a notify message to join/leave the multicast group. The current flow N2 -> N12/N13 -> N14/N15 reverses the required notification order and does not clearly represent the notify action as the trigger for the join/leave event.
prioritized_defects.evidence: Requirement R10 says 'An agent sends notify to join multicast group' and R11 says 'An agent sends notify to leave multicast group'. In the diagram, E5/E6 go from Select communication type to Join multicast group / Leave multicast group, then E16/E17 go from those actions to Send notify to join multicast group / Send notify to leave multicast group.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Reverse the causal ordering so that the notify actions occur before or as part of the join/leave operation, or model a single notification action that directly represents joining or leaving the multicast group.
Connect all diagram nodes to the main workflow.

prioritized_defects.description: The encryption/decryption path allows the decryption action to be reached from an unencrypted branch through the shared receive node, which conflicts with the requirement that decryption occurs only if the message is encrypted.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R14 and R17 state 'Message is decrypted only if Message is encrypted.' The diagram routes the 'Not encrypted' branch from N3 to N6 (E11), then from N6 to N7 via a guard 'Unicast or Multicast' (E13), and then to decryption completion (E15). This creates a path where an unencrypted message can still reach the decryption action node.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Separate the encrypted and unencrypted paths so that only the encrypted branch reaches the decryption action, and the not-encrypted branch bypasses decryption entirely.

prioritized_defects.description: The broadcast branch does not explicitly model the required delivery behavior to other agents in the same local network. Node N10 represents sending broadcast, but the corresponding receive behavior R21 is only reached through the encryption decision flow and is not directly tied to the broadcast-specific branch.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R20 requires 'An agent sends message to everyone in the same local network' and R21 requires 'Other agent in the same local network receive message'. The diagram has N10 -> N3 (E9), but the broadcast-specific receive is only attached via N6 -> N16 (E14) and N11 -> N16 (E21), with N11 not reached from the broadcast path directly.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Connect the broadcast send branch to the broadcast receive behavior explicitly, ensuring the local-network recipients are modeled as part of the broadcast flow and not only as a detached terminal node.

final_recommendation: Address D1 and D-STRUCT-003 in the next repair batch first, since they are the highest-severity issues and most likely to block correct workflow interpretation. Then tackle D2, followed by D3.
